resolutionSummary: Production Kentridge combat previously had no battle-progression authority after proximity activation: the CombatService only supported movement plus manual completion. Added authoritative HP, turn-consuming attacks, terminal team evaluation, a fixed-seed AI battle driver for both teams, Kentridge autonomous stepping/teardown, and high-signal terminal diagnostics. Exact-SHA CI passed all three focused regressions, including repeated fixed-seed completion and an exact Kentridge scene no-progress watchdog, and the same SHA built and ran KentridgePlayableSlice in the standalone player for 30 seconds with exit status 0 and zero harness assertion failures.

issues.title: Kentridge combat can freeze before battle completion
issues.description: Combat in Kentridge can enter a frozen or stalled state where the battle no longer advances. This blocks battle completion and makes combat progression unreliable. Fix the underlying stall and add a full end-to-end regression that runs a battle with AI controlling both sides from battle start through a terminal result.
issues.expected: A Kentridge battle must progress autonomously with AI controlling every combatant on both teams, never stall waiting for player input or an unresolvable turn state, reach a deterministic terminal victory/defeat condition within a bounded number of turns/actions, and cleanly exit or settle the combat state. The automated test must fail on any hang, stalled turn/phase, repeated no-progress state, missing terminal outcome, unhandled error, or timeout.
evidence: User report: combat in Kentridge freezes and does not complete.
Current coverage does not prove that a complete battle can run to a terminal outcome with AI controlling both sides.
Exact-SHA PlayMode fixture passed 3/3 cases. The exact-scene battle regression emitted: [KentridgeCombat] battle-complete seed=20260829 winner=Enemy actions=4 turns=1 pending=False.

The same tested SHA built Assets/Scenes/KentridgePlayableSlice.unity and ran the standalone player for 30 seconds with exit status 0, zero harness assertion failures, no runtime exception/error lines, and three inspected screenshots.
actions: Reproduce the Kentridge combat freeze and identify the exact turn/state transition where forward progress stops.
Fix the battle-flow, AI, or combat-state-machine defect causing the stall rather than masking it with retries or a larger timeout.
Add a deterministic full-battle automated regression with a fixed RNG seed that starts a representative Kentridge battle with AI controlling both teams and runs without player input.
Assert forward progress through turns, phases, and actions, with a bounded watchdog so any no-progress loop or hang fails loudly instead of counting a still-running process as success.
Assert the battle reaches a valid terminal outcome in which one side wins and the other loses within a bounded action or turn count.
Assert combat teardown completes cleanly and the game exits or settles the combat state with no pending AI action, turn, animation, target-selection wait, or other unresolved combat work.
Capture high-signal diagnostics on failure, including RNG seed, turn/action number, active unit and team, combat phase/state, pending action/target, and terminal-condition inputs.
Run the full-battle regression repeatedly through the normal headless test path to prove it is stable and not dependent on timing or a lucky seed.
Validate the exact Kentridge battle in the built application after the automated regression is green; demonstrate that AI can control both sides through battle completion without a freeze.
